items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Consumer sovereignty"?
items.answer: The idea that consumers decide what is produced through their choices.
items.markingKey: (a) Consumer sovereignty: The idea that consumers decide what is produced through their choices.
options: The idea that consumers decide what is produced through their choices.
Measures to protect consumers from unfair trade practices and to educate them about their rights and responsibilities.
Mixing inferior or harmful substances with a product.
A deceptive method used to promote the sale of goods or services, such as a false claim about quality.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the reasons why consumer protection is important from the point of view of business?
items.answer: Consumer ignorance
items.markingKey: (a) "Consumer ignorance" is one of the reasons why consumer protection is important from the consumers' point of view, not one of the reasons why consumer protection is important from the point of view of business.

items.stem: Explain the following ways and means of consumer protection: (i) Business associations (ii) Government.
items.answer: (i) Business associations: Bodies such as FICCI and CII lay down codes of conduct for members. (ii) Government: It passes laws such as the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Bodies such as FICCI and CII lay down codes of conduct for members. (ii) It passes laws such as the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

items.stem: Pillai Brothers treats customers fairly because satisfied customers come back and bring others. Which point of importance of consumer protection is shown?
items.answer: Long-term interest of business
items.markingKey: (b) Long-term interest of business. Satisfied customers mean repeat sales.

items.stem: Nair Agencies recognises its duty towards consumers as one of its stakeholders. Which point of importance of consumer protection is shown? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Social responsibility. Business is responsible to consumers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Social responsibility; 2 marks for the justification: Business is responsible to consumers.

items.stem:
Harleen bought a pack of rice from Singh Enterprises that was below the stated weight. She did not know where to complain, and other buyers in Lucknow faced the same problem but did nothing.
(i) Identify two reasons why consumer protection is important from the consumers' point of view. (ii) Why should Singh Enterprises protect consumers? Give two reasons.
items.answer: (i) Consumer ignorance; unorganised consumers (also widespread exploitation). (ii) Long-term interest of business; social responsibility; moral justification; to avoid government intervention (any two).
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Consumer ignorance; unorganised consumers (also widespread exploitation). (ii) Long-term interest of business; social responsibility; moral justification; to avoid government intervention (any two).

items.stem: Which of the following is one of the reasons why consumer protection is important from the consumers' point of view?
items.answer: Unorganised consumers
items.markingKey: (a) "Unorganised consumers" is one of the reasons why consumer protection is important from the consumers' point of view; the others are reasons why consumer protection is important from the point of view of business.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the reasons why consumer protection is important from the consumers' point of view?
items.answer: Business uses society's resources
items.markingKey: (a) "Business uses society's resources" is one of the reasons why consumer protection is important from the point of view of business, not one of the reasons why consumer protection is important from the consumers' point of view.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about consumer protection is correct?
items.answer: Business associations can lay down codes of conduct for their members.
items.markingKey: (b) Correct: Business associations can lay down codes of conduct for their members.
options: Consumers in India are well organised against exploitation.
Business associations can lay down codes of conduct for their members.
Only the government can protect consumers.
Social responsibility does not cover consumers.

items.stem: State any three ways and means of consumer protection.
items.answer: Self-regulation by business; Business associations; Consumer awareness; Consumer organisations; Government
items.markingKey: Any three of: Self-regulation by business; Business associations; Consumer awareness; Consumer organisations; Government (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Right to consumer education"?
items.answer: The right to acquire knowledge and skills to be an informed consumer.
items.markingKey: (d) Right to consumer education: The right to acquire knowledge and skills to be an informed consumer.
options: The right to file a complaint and to have the grievance considered at appropriate forums.
The right to complete information about the product, such as ingredients, price, date of manufacture and quality.
The right to be protected against goods and services that are hazardous to life and property.
The right to acquire knowledge and skills to be an informed consumer.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the rights of a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
items.answer: Buy only standardised goods
items.markingKey: (a) "Buy only standardised goods" is one of the responsibilities of a consumer, not one of the rights of a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

items.stem: Explain the following rights of a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019: (i) Right to be informed (ii) Right to safety.
items.answer: (i) Right to be informed: Complete information on the label about contents, price and expiry. (ii) Right to safety: Protection against hazardous goods, such as poor-quality electrical appliances.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Complete information on the label about contents, price and expiry. (ii) Protection against hazardous goods, such as poor-quality electrical appliances.

items.stem: Om is buying an electric heater. Which standard mark should the consumer look for?
items.answer: ISI mark
items.markingKey: (b) ISI mark. ISI is the standard mark for electrical and industrial goods.

items.stem: A shopkeeper in Chandigarh forced Karthik to buy only one brand of cooking oil. Which consumer right is involved? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Right to choose. Freedom to choose among products.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Right to choose; 2 marks for the justification: Freedom to choose among products.

items.stem: Which standard mark should the consumer look for? In each case give a reason. (i) Lakshmi is buying a pack of honey. (ii) Lakshmi is buying an electric geyser.
items.answer: (i) Agmark: Agmark is the mark for agricultural products. (ii) ISI mark: It is an electrical appliance.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Agmark (ii) ISI mark

items.stem: The packet of medicine bought by Harleen did not show its date of manufacture and price. (i) Which consumer right is involved? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Right to be informed: Details must be on the label. (ii) Any two of: label shows contents and price; date of manufacture and expiry; information helps in comparing products
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: label shows contents and price; date of manufacture and expiry; information helps in comparing products

items.stem:
Aditi bought a pressure cooker without the ISI mark and without taking a bill. It burst and injured her.
(i) Which right of the consumer was violated? (ii) State two responsibilities Aditi failed to perform.
items.answer: (i) Right to safety. (ii) Buy only standardised goods (ISI mark); ask for a cash memo.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Right to safety. (ii) Buy only standardised goods (ISI mark); ask for a cash memo.

items.stem: Tara got a new washing machine in place of the defective one sold by Mishra Stores, after the Commission's order. Which consumer right is involved?
items.answer: Right to seek redressal
items.markingKey: (a) Right to seek redressal. She got relief (replacement).

items.stem: An electric iron bought by Meera gave her a shock because it did not meet safety standards. (i) Which consumer right is involved? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Right to safety: Protection against hazardous goods. (ii) Any two of: protection against hazardous goods; standard marks such as ISI help ensure safety; covers life and property
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: protection against hazardous goods; standard marks such as ISI help ensure safety; covers life and property

items.stem: An electric iron bought by Diya gave her a shock because it did not meet safety standards. Which consumer right is involved?
items.answer: Right to safety
items.markingKey: (d) Right to safety. Protection against hazardous goods.

items.stem: Riya got a new washing machine in place of the defective one sold by Rao Enterprises, after the Commission's order. (i) Which consumer right is involved? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Right to seek redressal: She got relief (replacement). (ii) Any two of: replacement of defective goods; refund of price; compensation for loss or injury
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: replacement of defective goods; refund of price; compensation for loss or injury

items.stem: The label on the pack of ready-to-eat noodles did not mention the expiry date. (i) Which consumer right is involved? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Right to be informed: Complete product information must be given. (ii) Any two of: label shows contents and price; date of manufacture and expiry; information helps in comparing products
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: label shows contents and price; date of manufacture and expiry; information helps in comparing products

items.stem: State any three features of the three-tier redressal machinery.
items.answer: District Commission; State Commission; National Commission; Appeal from the District Commission; Appeal from the State Commission; Appeal from the National Commission
items.markingKey: Any three of: District Commission; State Commission; National Commission; Appeal from the District Commission; Appeal from the State Commission; Appeal from the National Commission (1 mark each).

items.stem: Explain the following persons who can file a complaint: (i) A legal heir or representative of a deceased consumer (ii) Any registered consumers' association.
items.answer: (i) A legal heir or representative of a deceased consumer: On behalf of the consumer who has died. (ii) Any registered consumers' association: A voluntary consumer association registered under law.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) On behalf of the consumer who has died. (ii) A voluntary consumer association registered under law.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the redressal machinery under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 is NOT correct?
items.answer: A complaint cannot be filed against a service provider.
items.markingKey: (a) Incorrect statement: A complaint cannot be filed against a service provider.
options: A complaint cannot be filed against a service provider.
The redressal machinery has three tiers: District, State and National Commissions.
A complaint can be filed against a seller, manufacturer or service provider.
An appeal against an order of the State Commission lies with the National Commission.

items.stem: A state government wants to act against a firm selling unsafe stationery to many consumers. Who can file a complaint in this situation?
items.answer: The Central or a State Government
items.markingKey: (b) The Central or a State Government. Governments can file complaints in the interest of consumers.
options: The Central or a State Government
The legal heir of a deceased consumer

items.stem: Sneha died because of a spurious medicine; her family wants to file a complaint. Who can file a complaint in this situation? Justify your answer.
items.answer: The legal heir of a deceased consumer. The legal heir can file on behalf of the deceased.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying The legal heir of a deceased consumer; 2 marks for the justification: The legal heir can file on behalf of the deceased.

items.stem:
Yash bought a laptop for ₹70,000 from Mishra Agencies; it stopped working in a week and Mishra Agencies refused to repair it. Yash took the matter to the District Commission, but was not satisfied with its order.
(i) Was Yash right to approach the District Commission? (ii) Where can he appeal, and within what time?
items.answer: (i) Yes: the value of the goods was within the District Commission's limit. (ii) To the State Commission, within 45 days of the order.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Yes: the value of the goods was within the District Commission's limit. (ii) To the State Commission, within 45 days of the order.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the redressal machinery under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 is correct?
items.answer: A complaint can be filed against a seller, manufacturer or service provider.
items.markingKey: (b) Correct: A complaint can be filed against a seller, manufacturer or service provider.
options: A complaint cannot be filed against a service provider.
A complaint can be filed against a seller, manufacturer or service provider.
The National Commission hears complaints of any value, however small.
An appeal against an order of the District Commission lies with the Supreme Court.

items.stem: A company paid ₹5 crore for defective machinery from Reddy Industries (Act as enacted). Which body should hear the matter?
items.answer: State Commission
items.markingKey: (a) State Commission. The value is above ₹1 crore and up to ₹10 crore.

items.stem: A registered voluntary consumer group in Chandigarh wants to file a complaint against adulteration. Who can file a complaint in this situation?
items.answer: Any registered consumers' association
items.markingKey: (b) Any registered consumers' association. Registered associations can file complaints.
options: The parent or legal guardian of a minor
The legal heir of a deceased consumer

items.stem: State any three remedies available to the consumer.
items.answer: To remove the defect in the product; To replace the defective product; To refund the price paid; To pay compensation for loss or injury; To pay punitive damages in appropriate circumstances; To remove the deficiency in service; To discontinue an unfair or restrictive trade practice; To stop the sale of hazardous goods; To withdraw hazardous goods from sale; To issue a corrective advertisement
items.markingKey: Any three of: To remove the defect in the product; To replace the defective product; To refund the price paid; To pay compensation for loss or injury; To pay punitive damages in appropriate circumstances; To remove the deficiency in service; To discontinue an unfair or restrictive trade practice; To stop the sale of hazardous goods; To withdraw hazardous goods from sale; To issue a corrective advertisement (1 mark each).

items.stem: Explain the following functions of consumer organisations and NGOs: (i) Filing cases in the interest of the general public (ii) Filing complaints in consumer commissions on behalf of consumers.
items.answer: (i) Filing cases in the interest of the general public: Not just for individual consumers. (ii) Filing complaints in consumer commissions on behalf of consumers: They act for consumers who cannot do so themselves.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Not just for individual consumers. (ii) They act for consumers who cannot do so themselves.

items.stem: Mishra Traders was ordered to stop forcing buyers of handicrafts to buy another product along with it. Which remedy has the Commission ordered?
items.answer: To discontinue an unfair or restrictive trade practice
items.markingKey: (b) To discontinue an unfair or restrictive trade practice. The practice must stop.
options: To pay compensation for loss or injury
To discontinue an unfair or restrictive trade practice
To withdraw hazardous goods from sale
To remove the defect in the product

items.stem: Because Mehta Industries knowingly sold spurious medicines, the Commission ordered heavy damages beyond the actual loss. Which remedy has the Commission ordered? Justify your answer.
items.answer: To pay punitive damages in appropriate circumstances. Damages punish the wrongdoer.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying To pay punitive damages in appropriate circumstances; 2 marks for the justification: Damages punish the wrongdoer.

items.stem: Singh Brothers, which falsely claimed its drink increases height, was told to publish a new advertisement correcting the claim. (i) Which remedy has the Commission ordered? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) To issue a corrective advertisement: It neutralises the misleading claim. (ii) Any two of: removes the effect of a misleading advertisement; paid for by the guilty party; protects other consumers
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: removes the effect of a misleading advertisement; paid for by the guilty party; protects other consumers

items.stem: Which of the following statements about remedies and consumer organisations is correct?
items.answer: A corrective advertisement neutralises the effect of a misleading advertisement.
items.markingKey: (d) Correct: A corrective advertisement neutralises the effect of a misleading advertisement.
options: A Commission can only order an apology from the seller.
Punitive damages are paid to the seller.
A corrective advertisement neutralises the effect of a misleading advertisement.

items.stem: A consumer group in Pune tested ten brands of bottled water in an accredited laboratory and published the results. (i) Which function of consumer organisations is performed? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Comparative testing of consumer products: Products are tested and compared. (ii) Any two of: done in accredited laboratories; results are published; helps consumers choose
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: done in accredited laboratories; results are published; helps consumers choose

items.stem: A consumer organisation brings out a monthly magazine on consumer problems. Which function of consumer organisations is performed?
items.answer: Publishing periodicals and other publications
items.markingKey: (a) Publishing periodicals and other publications. Knowledge is spread through publications.
options: Filing complaints in consumer commissions on behalf of consumers
Educating the public about consumer rights

items.stem: Which of the following statements about consumer rights and responsibilities is correct?
items.answer: Hallmark is the quality mark for gold jewellery.
items.markingKey: (d) Correct: Hallmark is the quality mark for gold jewellery.
options: Agmark is the standard mark for electrical goods.
A person who buys goods for resale is a consumer under the Act.

Hallmark is the quality mark for gold jewellery.

items.stem: What is meant by "Punitive damages"?
items.answer: Compensation awarded to punish the wrongdoer, in addition to compensation for loss.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Compensation awarded to punish the wrongdoer, in addition to compensation for loss.

items.stem: A firm wants to appeal against an order of the National Commission. Which body should hear the matter?
items.answer: Supreme Court
items.markingKey: (a) Supreme Court. Appeals against National Commission orders go to the Supreme Court.

items.stem: Explain the following reasons why consumer protection is important from the point of view of business: (i) Long-term interest of business (ii) Moral justification.
items.answer: (i) Long-term interest of business: Satisfied customers bring repeat sales and goodwill. (ii) Moral justification: It is the moral duty of business to avoid exploitation.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Satisfied customers bring repeat sales and goodwill. (ii) It is the moral duty of business to avoid exploitation.

items.answer: Government intervention

items.answer: (i) To stop the sale of hazardous goods: Hazardous goods are not offered for sale. (ii) To pay compensation for loss or injury: The consumer is compensated for loss suffered.

items.stem: Which of the following is one of the rights of a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
items.answer: Right to safety
items.markingKey: (b) "Right to safety" is one of the rights of a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019; the others are responsibilities of a consumer.

items.stem: A consumer organisation filed a complaint on behalf of an elderly buyer who could not go to the Commission. Which function of consumer organisations is performed?
items.answer: Filing complaints in consumer commissions on behalf of consumers
items.markingKey: (a) Filing complaints in consumer commissions on behalf of consumers. It acts on behalf of consumers.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about consumer protection is NOT correct?
items.answer: Social responsibility does not cover consumers.

Business associations can lay down codes of conduct for their members.

items.stem:
A child was injured by a defective toy bought from Thakur Retail; a registered consumer group and the state government also want to act, as many children have been hurt.
(i) Who can file complaints in the case? (ii) Describe the three-tier redressal machinery.
items.answer: (i) The parent or legal guardian of the minor; the registered consumers' association; the State Government; one or more consumers on behalf of numerous consumers. (ii) District Commission (value up to ₹1 crore as enacted), State Commission (₹1–10 crore, and appeals from District), National Commission (above ₹10 crore, and appeals from State); appeal from the National Commission to the Supreme Court.
items.markingKey: 6 marks: (i) The parent or legal guardian of the minor; the registered consumers' association; the State Government; one or more consumers on behalf of numerous consumers. (ii) District Commission (value up to ₹1 crore as enacted), State Commission (₹1–10 crore, and appeals from District), National Commission (above ₹10 crore, and appeals from State); appeal from the National Commission to the Supreme Court.

Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.

items.stem: What is meant by "Adulteration"?
items.answer: Mixing inferior or harmful substances with a product.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Mixing inferior or harmful substances with a product.

items.stem:
Meera bought a pressure cooker without the ISI mark and without taking a bill. It burst and injured her.
(i) Which right of the consumer was violated? (ii) State two responsibilities Meera failed to perform.
items.answer: (i) Right to safety. (ii) Buy only standardised goods (ISI mark); ask for a cash memo.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Right to safety. (ii) Buy only standardised goods (ISI mark); ask for a cash memo.

items.stem: Siddharth wants to appeal against an order of the District Commission. Which body should hear the matter? Justify your answer.
items.answer: State Commission. Appeals against District Commission orders go to the State Commission.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying State Commission; 2 marks for the justification: Appeals against District Commission orders go to the State Commission.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the responsibilities of a consumer?
items.answer: Right to be heard
items.markingKey: (b) "Right to be heard" is one of the rights of a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, not one of the responsibilities of a consumer.

items.stem: A consumer group gave free legal advice to Nikhil to fight his case against Sethi Retail. Which function of consumer organisations is performed? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Providing legal assistance to consumers. Legal help is given.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Providing legal assistance to consumers; 2 marks for the justification: Legal help is given.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "The consumer disputes redressal body at the state level, consisting of a President and not less than four members."
items.answer: State Commission
items.markingKey: (b) State Commission: The consumer disputes redressal body at the state level, consisting of a President and not less than four members.
